title: Mixed-fleet k8s bootstrap & upgrade playbook (bare-metal + vSphere) - draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic playbook for bootstrapping and performing control-plane and node upgrades for mixed fleets: vSphere-managed VMs + bare-metal nodes. Focus is on minimal blast radius, repeatable Terraform modules, preflight checks, and fast rollback paths.

Scope / assumptions:
- Cluster will have mixed node classes: control-plane on vSphere (VMs) and workers split between vSphere and bare-metal racks.
- Networking: L2/VLAN-backed fabric. MetalLB in layer2 mode for external LB where needed.
- PXE + iPXE flow for baremetal provisioning; vSphere uses cloud-init based templates.
- Storage: prefer Rook-Ceph for cross-node resilience; some worker pools may use local-ssd for ephemeral workloads.
- We use Terraform to describe infra (vSphere resources, BMC/IPMI resources, PXE configs).
- kubeadm used for bootstrap and upgrades (explicitly documented commands here).
- This is a working doc: TODOs inline, commands are examples not authoritative.

Inventory checklist (one-off before bootstrap):
- BMC access confirmed for all bare-metal nodes (IP, creds stored in vault).
- vSphere template names and customization specs verified (template-os: ubuntu-22.04-cloudimg).
- DHCP range reserved for PXE provisioning; TFTP and HTTP boot server IP set.
- Load balancer planned (HAProxy/NSX/physical LB) for control-plane endpoint.
- Certificate lives: cluster CA generated during kubeadm init unless customer requires central PKI.

Terraform module notes (high level):
- Module layout (recommended):
  - modules/vsphere/vm - creates templates, clones, customization spec bindings
  - modules/baremetal/node - creates ipmi/bmc records, PXE DHCP host reservations, ignition templates
  - modules/network - vlan/subnet allocation, metalLB config placeholders
  - modules/bootstrap - generates cloud-init/ignition artifacts and exposes bootstrap kubeadm-config as output

- Important variables to expose from modules:
  - control_plane_replicas (string -> int)
  - node_pools (list of objects: {name, role, count, flavor, disk_type, taints})
  - pxe_boot_server (string)
  - bmc_credentials_secret (vault path)

- Outputs to keep: 
  - control_plane_ips (list)
  - bootstrap_kubeconfig_path (string)
  - ignition_urls (map by node_pool)

- Implementation notes / pitfalls we ran into: 
  - DO NOT store raw BMC creds in tfstate; use Vault provider + template_file that fetches secret at plan time only (still careful!).
  - Keep IP allocation idempotent: use external ipam state (or a terraform resource with lifecycle ignore_changes for lease counters) otherwise repeated apply moves addresses.

Bootstrap phase (happy path):
1) Prep infra resources (terraform plan/apply stage 1): DNS zones, VLANs, LB placeholder, vSphere templates imported (readonly).
   - example: terraform apply -target=module.network -target=module.vsphere.template -var-file=env/prod.tfvars
2) Provision control-plane VMs (vSphere) in a canary set of 1 -> verify, then scale to 3.
   - cloud-init/bootstrap script will register an initial control-plane node but we prefer using kubeadm init on the first VM with external LB configured.
3) Configure control-plane external VIP and verify API endpoint reachable (kubectl --kubeconfig=/path to config get nodes).
4) Provision bootstrap worker on bare-metal (single bare-metal worker) using PXE and ignition URL. Ensure kubelet registers as worker.
5) Apply cluster addons (CNI, storage, ingress) in a staging namespace then promote to cluster-level:
   - install Calico/Weave/other (note: pick CNI that supports mixed MTU and host routes).
   - install MetalLB (layer2) for clusters without external load balancer.
6) Run functional smoke tests (see smoke tests section). If green, scale out additional pools.

vSphere-specific notes:
- Use customization spec to inject the machine-id and cloud-init token that pulls ignition from HTTP server.
- Template naming convention: redwood-k8s-ubuntu-22-<image-hash>. Keep tags on templates to avoid accidental reimport.
- vSphere SDK rate limits: when doing mass create of VMs, stagger clones by 10s and monitor tasks.

Bare-metal provisioning notes (PXE + iPXE + Ignition):
- PXE server actors: dnsmasq for DHCP/TFTP + nginx for HTTP artifact serving.
- iPXE flow: chainload -> kernel + initramfs + ignition URL parameter.
- BMC automation: use ipmitool or racadm in terraform null_resource to power-cycle nodes after provisioning.
- Hardware variance checklist: NIC driver versions, BIOS firmware baseline, CPU microcode. If a node fails to boot to kernel, collect console logs via BMC serial-over-LAN.

Networking and service exposure:
- Control-plane LB: HAProxy in front of 3 control-plane VMs (or external physical LB). Point kubeadm init --control-plane-endpoint to the VIP.
- Pod networking: Calico in BGP mode preferred for multi-rack performance, but requires AS planning. If BGP not feasible, use VXLAN mode and tune MTU.
- External services: MetalLB + NodePort fallback for emergency.

Storage considerations:
- Rook-Ceph recommended for mixed fleets. For racks with local-ssd, tag nodes with label storage=local-ssd and create a StorageClass 'local-ssd' for ephemeral workloads.
- During upgrades, PVCs on local storage will be disrupted; mark workloads accordingly.

Upgrade playbook (control-plane first, then workers):
Pre-upgrade checklist (run from SRE laptop, persist results):
- Verify backups: etcd snapshot successful (store in remote blob). Command: sudo ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/pre-upgrade-snap.db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/peer.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/peer.key
- Confirm CI e2e/smoke test pass on staging for target kubernetes minor version.
- Confirm kubeadm images available in internal registry or accessible (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler).
- Node readiness: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep -v Ready -> must be zero.

Control-plane upgrade (canary then roll):
1) Identify canary control-plane node (prefer vSphere VM with least pods) -> cordon it: kubectl cordon cp-01
2) SSH into cp-01, run: sudo kubeadm upgrade apply v1.27.6 --config /etc/kubernetes/kubeadm-config.yaml
3) Verify components: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l component=kube-apiserver
4) Run etcd health and snapshot verification.
5) If OK, uncordon and repeat sequentially for remaining control-plane nodes.
6) If control-plane fails to become ready, scale down to previous snapshot restore procedure (see rollback).

Worker upgrade (rolling, parallelism=1-2 depending on workload):
- Strategy: cordon -> drain (respecting PDBs) -> kubeadm upgrade node -> uncordon.
- Example sequence for a bare-metal worker 'bm-01':
  kubectl cordon bm-01
  kubectl drain bm-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
  ssh core@bm-01 sudo kubeadm upgrade node --kubelet-version v1.27.6
  ssh core@bm-01 sudo systemctl restart kubelet
  kubectl uncordon bm-01

- Notes: For stateful sets with local storage, plan workload evictions or move to alternate nodes first.

Canary pattern for mixed fleets:
- Prefer to upgrade 1 control-plane VM (vSphere), 1 vSphere worker, then 1 bare-metal worker. Validate: API latency, pod start latency, tail errors in app logs.
- Monitor for 30-60 minutes at each canary step. If error rate increases > 3x baseline or control-plane mortgage errors appear, stop and rollback.

Smoke tests (quick):
- kubectl get componentstatuses; kubectl get cs (expect all healthy)
- curl -k https://<control-plane-vip>:6443/healthz
- Deploy test nginx deployment (3 replicas) with affinity across node_pools and verify scheduling and HTTP 200
- Run perf smoke: 50 concurrent pod starts (job) and measure time to ready; baseline recorded in /ops/baselines/latest.json

Rollback / restore plan (short):
- If control-plane corruption: restore etcd from pre-upgrade snapshot on the first control-plane node (kubeadm docs).
- If worker upgrade causes severe regressions: cordon the rest of the pool, re-image offending nodes to previous image via PXE template and rejoin with old kubelet version (documented in image manifest).
- Keep terraform modules versioned by tag so infra rollback to previous VM template is possible (terraform state + vSphere template snapshot).

Post-upgrade verification:
- Run full e2e test suite (long), run quality checks (latency, error-rate delta).
- Confirm node metrics and kubelet logs for 24 hours.
- Update runbook with any anomalies and postmortem if any serious incident.

Operational run checklist (daily/upgrade window):
- 00:00 - snapshot etcd and push to blobstore (automated via cron but verify before upgrade)
- 00:10 - run preflight script (see preflight commands below).
- 00:30 - start canary control-plane upgrade, monitor for 1h before continuing.

Preflight commands (examples):
- check nodes: kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, ready: .status.conditions[] | select(.type=="Ready") .status }'
- check PDBs: kubectl get pdb --all-namespaces
- check etcd health: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=<ep> endpoint health

Known issues / TODOs:
- TODO: add exact ipmitool commands per vendor (Dell iDRAC vs HPE iLO vs Supermicro BMC) (Priya)
- TODO: finalize terraform pattern for ip allocation (Mateo)
- Issue: Some Broadcom NICs on older blades require driver update to avoid flapping under CNI.
- TODO: automated post-upgrade smoke runbook -> link to CI job (Samir)

Notes for on-call / emergency contacts:
- Primary infra oncall: eng-sre pager (pager duty link internal)
- BMC escalation: hardware team (hw-support@redwood.ai)

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- kubeadm init with external LB (example):
  kubeadm init --control-plane-endpoint "lb.redwood.local:6443" --upload-certs --pod-network-cidr=10.244.0.0/16
- kubeadm join control-plane (example snippet output saved at /tmp/join-cmd.txt)
- Quick image list: docker.io/k8s.gcr.io/kube-apiserver:v1.27.6

End of playbook (draft) - comments welcome.

----
Quick sign-offs needed before any production run:
- Security: KMS/CA policy reviewed for etcd snapshots
- SRE: roll schedule and escalation confirmed
- Product owner: approved maintenance window
